summary: This Order rescinds the previous stamp-duty order dated 20 December 1982 and all amendments to it. From 4 April 2006, stamp duty applies to gifts, transfers of immovable property and specified court documents at the rates set out in the Schedule, including tiered rates based on value.

summary: This Order made stamp duty chargeable from 6 October 2006 on specified instruments, including affidavits, insurance policies, notary warrants, licences, credit-card claims, share certificates, mortgages, promissory notes, leases, hire-purchase agreements and receipts. summary: This Order exempts specified instruments from stamp duty from 6 October 2006, including affidavits requested by public officers, bonds and mortgages given by public officers, certain insurance policies, mortgages, leases, receipts, share certificates and court documents. As amended by later gazettes, including 2312/73, the exemptions also cover qualifying government, financial-sector and share transactions, certain credit-card claims, and specified leases involving the Colombo Port City Economic Commission. summary: As amended by Gazette 1478/07, the schedule under the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act now includes two additional categories: unit trust or mutual fund certificates, and specified instruments involving Regional Development Banks, including loan security documents. summary: This notice sets the approved accountant’s certificate and supporting account details required for income tax filings, including information on assets, income, expenses, shareholders and related companies. summary: This notice designates several types of transactions for the purposes of section 108(1)(b) of the Inland Revenue Act. summary: The share transaction levy charged under section 7 of the Finance Act, No. 5 of 2005, is designated as a prescribed tax for the purposes of the Inland Revenue Act. This determines how the levy is treated under the income tax rules, but the notice does not set a new payment deadline or other action.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: No effective date is stated in the document; the Ministry date of 2007-03-01 and publication date of 2007-03-05 have not been treated as effective dates.

summary: These regulations define which company projects qualify as a “specified undertaking” for the Section 17 income-tax exemption. Eligible projects include listed manufacturing, engineering, cold-storage or refrigerated transport, export production villages, offshore-company management or back-office operations, and projects with investment above Rs. 250 million. The company must provide evidence of its investment and must not reduce or withdraw that investment during the exemption period; otherwise, its profits and income become liable to income tax from the relevant year of assessment in which operations began.
audience: ["income taxpayers operating companies seeking the Section 17 exemption"]
notes: The document does not state an effective date, so the publication date has not been used.

summary: Companies engaged in specified infrastructure activities may qualify for an income tax exemption on their profits and income. The activities include airports, seaports, highways, railways, industrial parks, warehouses, sanitation and waste management, power, water services, urban housing or own center development, and hospitals; the exemption lasts 6 to 12 years depending on investment of Rs. 1,000 million or more, provided the investment is fully made within one year after commercial operations begin.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The Order states eligibility conditions for a tax exemption but does not state a separate effective date. The audience is narrowed to companies whose undertakings meet the specified infrastructure activity and investment conditions.

summary: This Order sets Value Added Tax at 5% on imports of listed fish products, chickpeas and green grams. VAT-registered businesses importing these goods must apply the 5% rate; the Order does not state a separate effective date.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses importing the listed goods"]
notes: The document specifies the tax rate and the goods covered but does not expressly state when the rate takes effect. The audience is narrowed from the Act-level candidates based on the Order's reference to imported goods.

summary: This order updates the product list under section 16(2)(c) of the Inland Revenue Act to cover Sri Lankan-origin tea bags, yoghurt and curd made from locally produced fresh milk, and chilli powder made from locally produced chillies. The latest amendment, 2036/23, rescinds the earlier version and replaces it with revised rules, including an option to use the prescribed calculations.

Gazette 2036/23 rescinds the earlier regulations and introduces replacement wording, but does not state a separate commencement date.

summary: This gazette expanded an optional Economic Service Charge turnover calculation method to businesses covered by regulations 03 or 04, for quarters starting on or after 1 April 2007. audience: ["businesses liable to the Economic Service Charge"]

summary: This gazette adds “Ready to Drink Milk made from the locally produced fresh milk” to the order published in Gazette No. 1502/5 of 19 June 2007. The document does not state any separate compliance deadline or explain the underlying tax treatment beyond making this amendment.

notes: The gazette does not state an effective date. The practical tax effect depends on the content of Gazette No. 1502/5, which is not included here.

summary: These transfer pricing regulations required taxpayers entering transactions with associated undertakings to determine arm’s-length prices using specified methods and to keep supporting records for five years. The regulations were rescinded by Gazette 1823/05 with effect from 1 April 2013, so they no longer apply after that date.

summary: For income tax purposes, the order treats listed services performed outside employment as services carried on in a profession or vocation, including accounting, tax advice, engineering, software development, health care, and several trades. summary: This order sets the taxable values for employee benefits provided by employers, effective from 1 April 2011. summary: This notice identifies named villages in nine districts for the purpose of Section 34(2)(r) of the Inland Revenue Act. It does not state a new filing, payment or other compliance deadline; its practical tax effect depends on the relief or rule provided by Section 34(2)(r).
audience: ["Income taxpayers connected with the villages listed in the Schedule"]
notes: The document does not reproduce Section 34(2)(r), so the precise tax consequence of identifying these villages cannot be determined from the notice alone. The Gazette is dated 30 May 2013 and published on 6 June 2013, but neither date is stated as the effective date.

summary: These regulations set the transfer-pricing rules for associated undertakings, including arm’s-length pricing methods and records that must be kept for international and certain other transactions. As amended by Gazette 1960/39, from 1 April 2015, associated undertakings with transactions of at least LKR 100 million had to submit transfer-pricing reports and a director, principal officer or precedent partner certificate with the income tax return. The regulations were later rescinded by Gazette 2104/04, effective 1 April 2018, and are no longer operative.
audience: ["Income taxpayers that are associated undertakings entering into international transactions", "Income taxpayers that are associated undertakings entering into transactions other than international transactions"]
notes: The original regulations operated from 1 April 2013 and rescinded Gazette 1546/10 from that date. Gazette 1960/39 amended regulations 9 and 10 with effect from 1 April 2015. Gazette 2104/04 later rescinded Gazette 1823/05, effective 1 April 2018, so the rules in this gazette, including the amendment, are superseded.

summary: The Commissioner General of Inland Revenue wrote off listed tax arrears owed by 11 named institutions, including Sri Lanka Transport Board depots, government bodies and other organisations. The write-off covers tax charged and levied on or before 31 December 2009 and took effect on 17 December 2013 under the Default Taxes (Special Provisions) Act.
audience: ["The 11 institutions listed in the Schedule that had the specified tax arrears already in default"]

summary: This regulation sets the tax treatment and required supporting information when income taxpayers prepare financial statements under Sri Lanka Financial Reporting Standards or Lanka Accounting Standards. It covers items such as depreciation, leases, revenue, financial instruments, impairment and foreign exchange, and requires specified schedules or reconciliations to be submitted with tax computations. It applies to years of assessment beginning on or after 1 April 2012, including adjustments to accounting figures when calculating taxable income.
audience: ["Income taxpayers that prepare financial statements under Sri Lanka Financial Reporting Standards or Lanka Accounting Standards"]

summary: This regulation changes how eligible persons or partnerships may calculate Economic Service Charge when they choose the turnover-based option. It applies different statutory rates to quarters ending on or before 31 March 2011, quarters ending on or before 31 March 2012, and quarters commencing on or after 1 April 2012, replacing the previous single-rate reference. The change is stated to apply to relevant quarters commencing on or after 1 April 2007.
audience: ["Businesses liable to the Economic Service Charge, specifically persons or partnerships engaged in trades or businesses referred to in regulations 03 or 04"]
notes: The gazette changes the rate references used for the optional turnover-based calculation and has stated application to periods beginning on or after 1 April 2007, despite publication in 2014.

summary: This Order originally set stamp duty on share certificates at Rs. 5 for every Rs. 1,000, or part thereof, of the shares’ aggregate open-market value at issue, transfer or assignment. That provision was rescinded by Gazette 1882/17, so the original share-certificate rate no longer applies as issued here. Gazette 1933/14 later amended the underlying Schedule by setting duty on bonds or mortgages at Rs. 1 per Rs. 1,000, or part thereof; it did not restore the rescinded share-certificate provision.
audience: ["parties to transfers and other stampable instruments involving shares, share certificates, bonds or mortgages", "notaries"]
notes: Gazette 1882/17 expressly rescinds Gazette 1864/02 and replaces item 06. Gazette 1933/14 subsequently refers to the 1864 amendment but changes item 07 instead. The supplied documents do not state an effective date for Gazette 1864/02; the date shown is its signing/publication date, not an expressly stated commencement date.

summary: This order set out how VAT on financial services was calculated, including the value-addition formula, economic-depreciation rules, applicable rates, return periods and supporting documents for businesses supplying financial services. It applied from 1 January 2014, but was rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2316/13 with effect from 1 October 2022; therefore, these rules are no longer the operative rules for periods from that date.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses supplying financial services in Sri Lanka, particularly licensed commercial banks, licensed specialised banks and registered finance companies"]
notes: The original order is superseded: Gazette 2316/13 rescinds Gazette 1868/10 effective 2022-10-01. The effective_date shown is the earliest obligation date stated in this document, not the date on which the rules ceased to apply.

summary: The order added a category for share certificates issued when an insurance company separates its long-term and general insurance businesses, subject to the stated value limit. As amended by Gazette 1889/48, item 32 now contains revised wording for that insurance-business separation, and a new item 33 covers share certificates issued after approved mergers, acquisitions or absorptions involving certain banks, finance companies or leasing companies.
audience: ["parties to the qualifying share certificates, within the Act-level category of parties to stampable instruments"]
notes: The document does not state an effective date. The position is summarised as amended by Gazette 1889/48, which replaced item 32 and added item 33.

summary: The stamp duty rule for item 06 is replaced. Share certificates issued following the issue, transfer or assignment of company shares attract duty of Rs. 5 for every Rs. 1,000 or part of Rs. 1,000 of the shares’ aggregate open-market value, as assessed by the relevant revenue official; the earlier Order published as Gazette 1864/02 is also rescinded.
audience: ["parties to transfers and other stampable instruments involving company shares", "notaries"]
notes: The document does not state a separate effective date. It amends the Order published in Gazette 1465/19, as last amended by Gazette 1809/19, and rescinds Gazette 1864/02.

summary: As amended by Gazette 1947/46 from 1 January 2016, the order replaces the existing item for insurance-company share certificates and adds coverage for certain share certificates issued after the consolidation of licensed banks, finance companies or leasing companies. It also covers claims for payment arising from Sri Lankan-merchant credit-card transactions made on or after 1 January 2016, whether card-present or card-not-present and in any currency. The practical effect of these schedule entries depends on what the original 2006 order provides for instruments listed in its Schedule.
audience: ["parties to other stampable instruments covered by the Schedule, including affected share certificates and credit-card claims", "notaries"]
notes: This gazette does not state an effective date. It is superseded in part by Gazette 1947/46: the later gazette adds items 34 and 35, with item 34 applying to credit-card transactions entered into during periods commencing on or after 1 January 2016. The original 2006 order is not supplied, so the document alone does not establish whether the listed instruments are exempt from stamp duty or subject to it.

summary: As amended by Gazette 1960/42, this notice requires the prescribed Part IA transfer-pricing disclosure form for income taxpayers’ transactions with associated undertakings. It covers disclosures by the taxpayer and certification by an approved accountant, including transaction details and the arm’s-length pricing methods used, for years of assessment beginning on or after 1 April 2015. The Part IA certificate originally inserted by this Gazette was replaced by the later notice.
audience: ["Income taxpayers with transactions with associated undertakings"]
notes: Gazette 1960/42 replaces the Part IA inserted by Gazette 1907/26. The summary reflects the amended position, while the effective date is the date stated in Gazette 1907/26 for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2015.

summary: This Gazette set out the registration, invoicing, credit-voucher, return-filing and record-keeping rules for businesses using the Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) scheme, including eligible exporters, project participants and their suppliers. The rules are no longer in force: they were rescinded by Gazette 1986/09 with effect from 1 January 2016 and replaced by new SVAT guidelines.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses that qualify for, or supply businesses qualifying for, the SVAT scheme"]
notes: The original Gazette does not state an effective date; its publication date is not used as one. The position described is superseded by Gazette 1986/09, which rescinds Gazette 1910/02 effective 2016-01-01 and issues replacement SVAT guidelines.

summary: Item 07 was replaced to set stamp duty on every bond or mortgage securing a definite and certain sum at Rs. 1 for every Rs. 1,000 or part of Rs. 1,000. As amended by Gazette 1947/45, this item 07 rate remains unchanged; that later Gazette replaced item 05 instead.
audience: ["parties to bonds and mortgages that secure a definite and certain sum of money", "notaries"]
notes: Gazette 1933/14 does not state an effective date. Gazette 1947/45 later amended the underlying Order by replacing item 05, but did not alter the item 07 rate covered here.

summary: Item 05 of the stamp-duty schedule was replaced for credit-card transactions entered into from 1 January 2016. A charge of Rs. 25 applies for every Rs. 1,000 or part of Rs. 1,000 claimed, demanded or requested, excluding finance and service charges, where the merchant country is outside Sri Lanka; this applies whether the card was present or not and in any currency.
audience: ["parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments", "notaries"]
notes: Gazettes 2091/03 and 2104/05 refer to this Order but amend item 04, not item 05, so no later change to the item 05 rate or scope is evident from the supplied documents.

summary: The order adds two categories to the Stamp Duty Schedule: claims, demands or requests for payment arising from Sri Lankan-merchant credit card transactions entered into on or after 1 January 2016, and share certificates issued following the issue, transfer or assignment of shares. Gazette 2007/24 later amended other Schedule items but did not change these additions, so this remains the position as amended. Businesses and notaries should assess the stamp-duty treatment of these transactions and documents from the stated date.
audience: ["parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments", "notaries"]
notes: The document adds items 34 and 35 to the Schedule but does not expressly state whether the listed instruments are chargeable or exempt; the summary therefore describes the Schedule change without asserting a specific duty outcome. Gazette 2007/24, effective 2017-02-21, substituted items 12, 15 and 16 only and did not alter items 34 or 35.

summary: As amended, the Order replaces Schedule I of Gazette 1791/08 and sets the charge for persons leaving Sri Lanka at US $30.00, whether they leave by aircraft or ship. The new schedule applies from 1 January 2016.
audience: ["travellers leaving Sri Lanka by aircraft", "travellers leaving Sri Lanka by ship"]
notes: This gazette amends the Order published in Extraordinary Gazette No. 1791/8 dated 31 December 2012. The document itself uses the typo “subsitution” in its amendment wording; it has not been reproduced in the summary.

summary: As amended, associated undertakings with transactions with other associated undertakings totalling at least Rs. 100 million in a year of assessment must submit transfer-pricing disclosures with their income tax return. Their director, principal officer or precedent partner must also submit a transfer-pricing certificate to the Commissioner General, with copies or inclusion in the company’s annual report as specified. The changes apply from 1 April 2015; where the relevant transactions are Rs. 10 million or less, the disclosure may generally be limited to the transaction records and related information.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: This gazette replaces regulations 9 and 10 of Gazette Extraordinary No. 1823/05. The document contains typographical errors, including “subtitution”, “categaries” and “Commisisoner”, but these do not affect the stated requirements.

summary: This notice replaces Part IA of Gazette Extraordinary No. 1907/26 with a revised transfer pricing disclosure form. Income taxpayers must use the form to report transactions with associated undertakings, including receipts, payments, loans, pricing methods, documentation, financial information and certification, for years of assessment beginning on or after 1 April 2015.
audience: ["Income taxpayers with transactions involving associated undertakings"]
notes: The notice does not state a filing deadline. The form requires certification by an approved accountant and refers to Transfer Pricing Regulations, but those documents were not supplied.

summary: This gazette set the operating rules for the Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) Scheme, including which qualifying businesses could register, how suspended VAT invoices and credit vouchers had to be handled, and the forms, records and return deadlines that applied. It replaced the earlier 1910/02 guidelines from 1 January 2016. As amended by 2456/02, the SVAT Scheme was later repealed and this gazette rescinded, with the Risk Based Refund Scheme applying from 1 October 2025.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses that qualified as Registered Identified Purchasers or Registered Identified Suppliers under the SVAT Scheme, including qualifying exporters, project suppliers and their suppliers"]
notes: The original rules are superseded from 2025-10-01 by Gazette 2456/02, which rescinds this gazette following the repeal of the SVAT Scheme and introduces the Risk Based Refund Scheme. The effective_date shown is the earliest obligation date stated in this gazette, not the later rescission date.

summary: From 1 November 2016, the cost of healthcare services listed in the Schedule is excluded when calculating the VAT value of a healthcare service. This exclusion does not cover fees paid to medical practitioners, medical consultation fees, channeling fees, or hospital room charges.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses supplying healthcare services"]
notes: The Schedule uses the spelling “practioners”; this summary preserves the substance rather than reproducing that typo.

summary: These regulations introduce electronic submission of tax returns, supporting documents and schedules through the Inland Revenue Department’s RAMIS web portal, in the format and manner specified by the Commissioner General. They also set rules for authorised staff and tax agents, system-generated notices and assessments, temporary acknowledgements, and electronic record storage. No commencement or effective date is stated in the document.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The regulations also refer to returns and documents under the Value Added Tax Act, National Building Tax Act and Economic Service Charge Act, but the supplied enabling Act is the Inland Revenue Act. The Commissioner General’s detailed web-portal procedures and formats are not included in the document.

summary: From 9 February 2017, new rules govern approval and registration of authorized representatives under the Inland Revenue Act. They set eligibility and disqualification requirements, require applicants to apply to the Commissioner General, and require an annual Gazette list of approved representatives. The rules replace the 2007 regulations and their 2011 amendment.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The regulations primarily impose requirements on individuals seeking or holding authorized-representative status, but that audience is not among the supplied Act-level candidates. “Income taxpayers” is therefore used as the closest affected audience because the rules govern who may represent them for Inland Revenue purposes.

summary: From 21 February 2017, the order changes which instruments are exempt from stamp duty: specified life, medical, construction/agriculture and motor-vehicle insurance policies, qualifying finance leases, and qualifying hire-purchase agreements. In practice, finance leases and hire-purchase agreements for Class B cars and dual-purpose motor vehicles are excluded from these exemptions. As amended by Gazette 2149/18, the order also covers certain non-cash government or Urban Development Authority land leases; that later gazette does not state a separate effective date.
audience: ["parties to stampable instruments, including insurance policies, finance leases, hire-purchase agreements and qualifying government or Urban Development Authority leases", "notaries"]
notes: The document is summarised as amended by Gazette 2149/18, which added item 36 concerning certain government or Urban Development Authority land leases. Gazette 2149/18 does not state an effective date, so the effective_date remains the date stated in this gazette. The supplied later-gazette information does not identify any further change to the substituted items 12, 15 and 16.

summary: From 2 May 2016, VAT-registered wholesalers and retailers may claim deemed input VAT on eligible opening stock and purchases from non-VAT-registered suppliers, subject to the stated limits. They must keep specified stock and purchase records, collect supplier documents, submit the required schedules with VAT returns, enter the amounts in the specified return fields, and submit a reconciliation with the Income Tax Return; the maximum retail price cannot be increased because of the credit.
audience: ["VAT-registered wholesalers and retailers"]
notes: The notification was published on 27 March 2017 but expressly states that it is effective from 2 May 2016. Specific eligibility periods and treatment differ for opening stock and purchases from non-VAT-registered persons.

summary: These regulations rescind and replace the earlier Economic Service Charge regulations published in Gazettes 1502/10, 1506/06 and 1546/09. They allow businesses in specified sectors to opt for prescribed quarterly turnover calculations, including special calculations for freight forwarders, certain exporters and primary dealers, and then calculate Economic Service Charge on that turnover. The document does not state a commencement or effective date.
audience: ["Businesses liable to the Economic Service Charge, particularly freight forwarders, certain exporters and primary dealers"]
notes: The regulations expressly rescind the earlier regulations without affecting anything already done under them. No effective or commencement date is stated in the document.

summary: These regulations replace the 1998 record-keeping rules and require every VAT-registered business to keep detailed, up-to-date records of taxable, exempt, excluded and suspended supplies, imports, purchases, adjustments and input/output tax. Businesses must maintain specified VAT control accounts, worksheets and schedules, submit the required schedules with VAT returns where applicable, and preserve records for five years after the relevant taxable period. The regulations also include special record and schedule requirements for RIPs, RISs and certain wholesale and retail businesses.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses, including Registered Identified Purchasers and Registered Identified Suppliers where applicable"]
notes: The gazette says the regulations operate effective for the requirement of the sections, but does not state a clear commencement date. The 2 May 2016, 1 November 2016 and 31 December 2010 dates in the text relate to specific deemed-input-credit and record requirements, not a general effective date. Gazette Extraordinary No. 1024/8 of 21 April 1998 is expressly rescinded.

summary: From 1 April 2018, banks and financial institutions must withhold income tax at 5% on a senior citizen’s interest income above Rs. 1,500,000 for the year of assessment. Senior citizens must submit a declaration each year for each account, stating whether the threshold is exceeded or the relief has already been used elsewhere; false or misleading declarations are treated as statements made to a tax official.
audience: ["income taxpayers who are resident senior citizens of Sri Lanka receiving bank or financial-institution interest", "withholding agents, including banks and financial institutions paying that interest"]
notes: The prescribed declaration form contains apparent typographical errors, including “Year f assessment,” “ineterest,” and “place withhold.”

summary: For section 85 of the Inland Revenue Act, these regulations prescribe categories of services treated as having a source in Sri Lanka when paid to a resident individual, including professional, construction, security, management, vocational and similar services. They also prescribe a 2% rate when a resident person makes a payment to a non-resident person. The regulations apply from 1 April 2018.
audience: ["withholding agents who are resident persons making payments covered by section 85"]
notes: The document's wording is grammatically unclear in describing services paid to a resident individual, but the listed service categories and the 2% rate for payments by a resident person to a non-resident person are stated expressly.

summary: From 1 April 2018, official emoluments paid to an individual employed by the Asian Development Bank are treated as exempt amounts for the purposes of the Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act. This means those emoluments are excluded from the relevant income-tax calculation.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]

summary: These transitional rules preserve certain tax exemptions, concessionary rates, losses, allowances, depreciation treatment, finance-lease calculations, approvals and notional tax credits when the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 replaced the earlier tax law from 1 April 2018. As amended by Gazette 2089/01 from 17 September 2018, qualifying enterprises with pre-April 2018 Board of Investment agreements may also continue their agreed exemptions or reduced rates for dividends paid by those enterprises.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The position is summarised as amended by Gazette 2089/01 (2018-09-17), which substitutes paragraph (3) and adds dividends covered by qualifying Board of Investment agreements. The effective date reported is the date stated in this gazette; the amendment's operative timing is not separately specified beyond its issue date.

summary: When calculating a person’s income, income taxpayers must not deduct the listed taxes and levies, including Economic Service Charge, certain taxes on financial services, Crop Insurance Levy, and specified levies under the Finance Act. Item (i) was later amended by Gazette 2130/02 to cover comparable income taxes paid in any country, subject to the foreign tax credit limitation, and applies from 1 April 2018.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The position is summarised as amended by Gazette 2130/02, which rescinded and replaced item (i) of this Gazette with effect from 1 April 2018. The effective date reported is the date stated in this Gazette.

summary: Losses on a financial instrument may be offset only against gains from the same type of financial instrument. This sets the required tax treatment for taxpayers reporting such financial instrument losses and gains.
audience: ["income taxpayers with losses or gains on financial instruments"]
notes: The notice is dated 1 April 2018 but does not state a separate effective date; the document’s wording is grammatically unclear, but its practical rule is that losses may be set off only against gains from the same type of financial instrument.

summary: This notice addresses the period used when interest on a blended loan is compounded. It says that another period recognised under generally accepted accounting principles is specified, but it does not identify that period in the document, so the practical calculation rule cannot be determined from this notice alone.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The notice refers to a period considered under generally accepted accounting principles but does not state the period itself. Applying the rule depends on the relevant accounting principles or another document not provided. The date shown is the department/signatory date, not an expressly stated effective date.

summary: The 2018 notice set limits on which provisions for debt claims a banking business could deduct when calculating taxable banking profits, including provisions for loans to associated persons or persons outside Sri Lanka. It was rescinded by Gazette 2303/05 with effect from 1 April 2022 and replaced by new specifications, which also exclude certain pawning, employee and multiple-facility claims and Stage 1 and Stage 2 impairment charges. The 2018 rule therefore no longer applies.
audience: ["income taxpayers conducting a banking business, including relevant financial institutions"]
notes: The 2018 notice does not state a separate effective date, so effective_date is null. Gazette 2303/05 rescinds it effective 1 April 2022; the summary reflects that superseding position, although that date belongs to the later gazette.

summary: From 1 April 2018, an income taxpayer may designate an authorized representative to communicate with the Inland Revenue Department in specified matters. These include registration and profile changes, tax returns, private rulings, reviews, refunds, extensions of time, investigations, capital gains tax returns, and any other matter specifically authorized in writing.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]

summary: People liable for Capital Gains Tax on investment assets realised on or after 1 April 2018 must submit the specified Capital Gain Tax return and schedules. The filing deadline is generally one month after the realisation; a separate rule applies when a resident individual’s total gains exceed Rs. 600,000, and joint ownership can require each resident individual to file. The prescribed forms are Annex I (Asmt_CGT_001_E) and Annex II (Asmt_CGT_002_E).
audience: ["Income taxpayers liable to pay Capital Gains Tax on gains from the realisation of investment assets, including resident individuals and resident individuals with jointly owned assets covered by the stated thresholds"]
notes: Part of the document, including pages containing the annex forms and schedules, is supplied only as machine-read text from page images and may contain OCR errors; some image content is missing. The summary relies on the readable operative text and does not independently verify all form fields or schedule details.

summary: From 1 April 2018, employers must withhold income tax from employee payments using the applicable tax table for regular pay, lump sums, terminal benefits, non-citizen employees, multiple or secondary employments, and tax paid by the employer on an employee’s behalf. Employers must also manage primary-employment declarations, issue withholding certificates, file annual employee and tax details, and keep relevant records for at least five years.
audience: ["employers", "withholding agents"]
notes: The gazette refers to Tax Tables 01–07, but the tables themselves are not included in the supplied document; the exact withholding rates therefore cannot be confirmed from this text alone.

summary: This notice sets the eligibility requirements for an individual to register as an authorized representative under the Inland Revenue Act, including age, Sri Lankan residency and citizenship, specified tax or accounting qualifications, experience and fitness requirements. It also provides for registration, removal from the register and annual publication of registered representatives. The requirements in this notice were replaced by Gazette 2194/50 on 23 September 2020; as amended, the replacement schedule also recognises Chartered Tax Advisors and changes some qualification wording.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The supplied later gazette, No. 2194/50 dated 2020-09-23, repeals and substitutes Schedule 01 rather than merely rescinding the notice. The summary states the amended position, but effective_date is the date stated in this original document as required.

summary: A taxpayer requesting a private ruling from the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue must pay a fee of Rs. 25,000.00 for the application. The notice does not state a separate commencement date, so the fee applies as specified in this notice from its publication date context.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The notice states the fee but does not expressly state an effective date. It is limited to applications for private rulings requested by a taxpayer.

summary: From 2 July 2018, the cost of healthcare services other than hospital room charges is excluded when calculating the value of healthcare supplies for VAT. This replaces and rescinds the earlier healthcare-services order published in Gazette No. 1991/17 dated 1 November 2016.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses supplying healthcare services"]

summary: Section 58A of the Value Added Tax Act comes into operation on 11 September 2018. This gazette only sets the commencement date; it does not explain the requirements contained in section 58A.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses"]
notes: The gazette does not describe the substance of section 58A, so any specific compliance requirements depend on the Act and amendments referred to in the document.

summary: This Gazette sets out the Tourist Value Added Tax Refund Scheme (TVRS). Tourists may claim a refund of 80% of the VAT-exclusive value of eligible goods taken out of Sri Lanka, provided the purchases total at least Rs. 50,000 excluding VAT, are covered by no more than three invoices per day, and are made from an Authorized Retailer. Bottled water, aerated water, cooked meals, and goods that have been fully or partly consumed are excluded.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses acting as Authorized Retailers", "Consumers, including tourists purchasing qualifying goods, indirectly through the refund scheme"]
notes: The document does not state an effective date for the scheme, so none is reported.

summary: This Order amends Gazette Extraordinary No. 2064/53. It preserves the tax treatment promised in qualifying agreements entered into with the Board of Investment before April 2018: the enterprise’s profits and income, and dividends it pays, remain exempt or continue to be taxed using the agreed basis or rate under the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The document does not state a separate effective date. The protected agreements must have been entered into before April 2018 and must contain the specified tax exemption, reduced-rate, or tax-computation provisions.

summary: This Order imposes VAT at 5% on the importation of the listed textile and fabric products, identified by their H.S. codes. It covers a wide range of silk, wool, cotton, flax, synthetic and artificial-fibre fabrics, knitted fabrics, lace, coated fabrics and related textile products.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses importing the listed goods"]
notes: The document is dated 17 September 2018 but does not expressly state an effective or commencement date; therefore effective_date is null.

summary: From 1 October 2018, item 04 stamp-duty rates for trade, business, professional and vocational licences were replaced: non-liquor licences were charged Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever was lower; most liquor licences Rs. 20,000; and specified arrack and bottled-toddy licences Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever was higher. Gazette 2091/03 was rescinded by Gazette 2104/05 with effect from 1 January 2019, which re-enacted these rates in a replacement item 04; this is the position as amended.
audience: ["parties to stampable instruments, including the specified trade, business, professional and vocational licence transactions", "notaries"]
notes: Gazette 2091/03 is superseded from 1 January 2019 by Gazette 2104/05, which rescinds it and substitutes a replacement item 04. The effective date reported is the date stated in this gazette; the amended position applies from 2019-01-01.

summary: VAT is charged at 5% on the supply or import of wood products under HS headings 4407 and 4408. This covers wood sawn, chipped, sliced or peeled to a thickness exceeding 6 mm, and specified veneering or plywood-related sheets over 6 mm thick.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses"]
notes: The Order does not state a separate effective date; the document is dated 2018-11-01. The 5% rate applies to the supply or import of the goods described in the Schedule.

summary: VAT is set at 0% on the importation of the listed woven, knitted and related textile fabrics under the specified H.S. codes. This Order rescinds the earlier Order published as Gazette No. 2089/13 dated 17 September 2018, so importers should use this schedule for the covered goods.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses importing the listed textile goods"]
notes: The document does not state a separate effective date; the date shown is the Order date and publication date. The listed rate is 0%, although the Order declares that VAT shall be charged.

summary: These regulations introduced transfer pricing rules for transactions between associated enterprises, requiring them to use arm’s-length pricing and keep supporting records. Affected taxpayers also had to submit transfer pricing information with their income tax return, with additional documentation requirements for larger transactions and multinational groups. The rules in this gazette were later rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2217/07, effective from 1 April 2020; the replacement applies for periods from that date.
audience: ["Income taxpayers carrying out controlled transactions with associated enterprises"]
notes: This gazette rescinded Gazette 1823/05 effective 1 April 2018. It was subsequently rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2217/07, which states that the replacement operates and the 2018 regulations are rescinded effective 1 April 2020. The summary therefore describes the position as amended, while the effective_date is the date stated in this gazette.

summary: From 1 January 2019, this Order changed stamp duty on specified trade, business, profession and vocation licences: non-liquor licences are charged Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever is lower; most liquor licences are charged Rs. 20,000; and certain listed liquor licences are charged Rs. 2,000 or 10% of the licence fee, whichever is higher. As amended by Gazette 2429/39 from 1 April 2025, stamp duty also applies to leases and hire agreements at Rs. 20 per Rs. 1,000 of the total amount for the term, or Rs. 10 per Rs. 1,000 for qualifying hire-purchase agreements.
audience: ["Parties to stampable instruments, particularly persons obtaining the specified trade, business, profession or vocation licences and parties to leases or hire agreements", "Notaries handling these stampable instruments"]
notes: The 2018 Order rescinds Gazette 2091/03 with effect from 1 January 2019. The position has subsequently been amended by Gazette 2429/39, effective 1 April 2025; that later Gazette replaces item 9 on lease and hire instruments but does not change the licence rates in item 04. The effective_date is the date stated in this 2018 document, not the later amendment date.

summary: This order imposed 5% VAT on specified services supplied by Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses, and on inbound tours supplied by registered travel agents, starting 21 May 2019. As amended by Gazette 2125/69, the 5% order was repealed from 1 June 2019 and replaced with a 7% rate for these services until 31 March 2020.
audience: ["VAT-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses registered with the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority", "VAT-registered travel agents registered with the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority supplying inbound tours"]
notes: The original 5% rate applied only from 21 May 2019 until its repeal effective 1 June 2019. The position stated here is as amended by Gazette 2125/69: 7% from 1 June 2019 to 31 March 2020.

summary: As amended by this Gazette, VAT is charged at 7% on services supplied by Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses, and on inbound-tour services supplied by registered travel agents. This rate applies from 1 June 2019 to 31 March 2020 and replaces the order published as Gazette 2124/03 from 1 June 2019.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses that are Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants or similar businesses", "VAT-registered travel agents supplying inbound tours"]
notes: This Gazette repeals the order published as Extraordinary Gazette Notification No. 2124/03 with effect from 1 June 2019 and sets the replacement rates for the stated period.

summary: This regulation replaces item (i) of the Schedule issued in Gazette 2064/54. The replacement covers income tax, super tax, surtax, or similar taxes paid in another country, while excluding any amount above the foreign tax credit allowed under sections 80 and 81 of the Inland Revenue Act. It applies from 1 April 2018.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: This Gazette repeals the specified item (i) in Gazette 2064/54 and substitutes the text quoted in this document.

summary: From 1 November 2019, VAT is charged at 6% on services involving the supply of residential accommodation by selling a condominium housing unit. This affects businesses that make these supplies and may indirectly affect consumers through the price charged.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses supplying residential accommodation through the sale of condominium housing units", "consumers indirectly, through prices"]

summary: This Order added a new Schedule item covering instruments for leases of land by the Government, government representatives or the Urban Development Authority where the lease premium or rent is not paid in cash and the agreement involves the Government. The position was later amended by Gazette 2312/73, which also covers qualifying leases of land in the Colombo Port City area by the Colombo Port City Economic Commission, from the commencement of the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act.
audience: ["parties to qualifying government, Urban Development Authority and Colombo Port City Economic Commission leases", "notaries"]
notes: Gazette 2149/18 does not state an effective date, so effective_date is null. The position is summarised as amended by Gazette 2312/73; that later Gazette refers to the commencement date of the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act but does not state the date itself.

summary: From 1 December 2019, VAT was set at 0% for qualifying services supplied by Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses where at least 60% of inputs came from local sources; financial services were taxed at 15%, specified imports at their listed rates, and most other imports, goods and services at 8%. The local-input definitions were added by Gazette 2152/60. This position was later rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2282/26 from 1 June 2022, which set the general rate for the covered imports, goods and services at 12%.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses, narrowed to tourism businesses supplying the qualifying services, financial service suppliers, importers, and suppliers of goods or services"]
notes: The original order is superseded as amended: Gazette 2152/60 added definitions relevant to the 0% tourism-services rate, while Gazette 2282/26 rescinded the order with effect from 2022-06-01 and replaced its rates. Gazette 2152/60 does not state a separate commencement date.

summary: As amended by Gazette 2152/60, the 0% VAT rule in paragraph 1(a) of Gazette 2151/52 uses a specified earlier taxable period to calculate total inputs. It also defines locally sourced inputs as spending on locally produced agricultural, horticultural, fishing, animal husbandry or dairy products, and locally manufactured goods with at least 10% local value addition.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses applying the 0% VAT rate under paragraph 1(a) of Gazette 2151/52"]
notes: The document does not state an effective date. The practical effect depends on the 0% VAT rule in paragraph 1(a) of Gazette 2151/52, which is not reproduced here.

summary: This notice replaces Schedule 01 in Gazette 2064/63 and sets the requirements for registering an individual as an authorized representative under the Inland Revenue Act. Applicants must generally be Sri Lankan citizens and residents aged at least 21, meet one of the listed professional or experience-based qualifications, and have none of the stated disqualifications. The Commissioner General may register or remove representatives and must publish the register at least once a year.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
authority: Nadun Guruge, Commissioner General of Inland Revenue
notes: The notice does not state an effective date. It rescinds and replaces Schedule 01 of Gazette Extraordinary No. 2064/63 dated 2018-04-01. The schedule directly concerns authorized representative applicants, but that category was not included among the supplied audience candidates; income taxpayers are therefore used as the closest Act-level audience.

summary: These regulations replace Gazette Extraordinary No. 2104/4 and apply from 1 April 2020. They require income taxpayers carrying out controlled transactions with associated enterprises to apply arm’s-length pricing and, where the stated thresholds apply, maintain transfer-pricing files, submit an annual disclosure form, and meet country-by-country reporting or notification requirements. They also set the recognised pricing methods, penalties for non-compliance, and rules for advance pricing agreements.
audience: ["income taxpayers carrying out controlled transactions with associated enterprises, including Sri Lankan-resident multinational enterprise group entities"]
notes: The regulations operate retrospectively from 1 April 2020 and rescind Gazette Extraordinary No. 2104/4 effective from the same date. The document contains several apparent typographical and drafting errors; the summary follows the operative requirements as printed.

summary: These guidelines explain how to calculate income tax for the 2019/2020 year of assessment after the 2021 amendments. Individuals must divide income and reliefs between the periods before and after 1 January 2020, while partnerships and other entities must apply the specified apportionment, tax rates, withholding-tax and tax-credit rules. Partnerships became liable for income tax on taxable income from 1 January 2020.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The guidelines apply specifically to the 2019/2020 year of assessment and contain separate rules for individuals, partnerships, and persons other than individuals and partnerships. The document also refers to the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 10 of 2021, but the supplied enabling Act is the Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017.

summary: This notice sets conditions for pension, provident, gratuity and savings funds approved by the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue. An employer’s total contributions to terminal-benefit funds, including EPF and ETF, must not exceed 25% of its total salary bill for the accounting year; approved funds must also meet specified investment limits. EPF and ETF are treated as approved funds regardless of these conditions.
audience: ["employers"]
notes: The notice does not state an effective date. The investment conditions apply to approved funds, while the supplied audience candidates do not include such funds as a separate category; employers are the clearest affected audience among the candidates.

summary: This Order prescribes information technology and enabled services for the tax treatment referred to in the Third Schedule of the Inland Revenue Act, effective from 1 January 2020. Businesses providing the listed services must meet conditions including, from 1 April 2020, a minimum 70% share of local technical employees for specified software services, or at least 50% local value addition for other listed services; businesses formed by splitting an existing business do not qualify.
audience: ["income taxpayers providing the prescribed information technology or enabled services", "employers operating businesses covered by the local-employee condition"]
notes: The Order takes effect from 1 January 2020, while the employee and local-value-addition conditions expressly apply from 1 April 2020.

summary: This Order, effective from 1 April 2021, identifies information technology and enabled services that qualify for the treatment under item (Liv) of the VAT Act’s First Schedule. Providers must meet conditions including a 70% local technical employee threshold for software-related services, at least 50% local value addition for most other listed services, and an exclusion for businesses created by splitting up an existing business. The underlying VAT treatment under item (Liv) is not reproduced in this Order.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses supplying the prescribed information technology and enabled services"]
notes: The Order refers to item (Liv) of paragraph (b) of Part II of the First Schedule, but that provision is not included in the supplied text; the exact VAT consequence therefore depends on the wording of that provision.

summary: This notice sets the method for calculating the local value added in goods and services for the additional deduction available for qualifying marketing and communication expenses. Businesses claiming that deduction must keep calculation worksheets, expense lists, supplier and associated-person details, contracts, and supporting invoices or tax invoices. It covers sellers of goods, manufacturers’ distributors undertaking marketing and communication, and service suppliers, including mixed or composite services.
audience: ["income taxpayers who intend to claim the additional deduction under the Sixth Schedule, including sellers of goods and suppliers of services"]
notes: The document does not state a commencement or effective date; the publication date has therefore not been used.

summary: This Order replaced the earlier VAT order and set VAT at 12% from 1 June 2022 for imports and supplies not covered by the specified imported-goods schedule. As amended by Gazette 2300/25, sanitary towels (pads) and tampons were made zero-rated from 7 October 2022; as amended by Gazette 2363/22, the general rate became 18% from 1 January 2024, and the 15% rate introduced by Gazette 2295/08 was rescinded.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses importing goods", "VAT-registered businesses supplying goods or services"]
notes: The position described is as amended by Gazettes 2300/25 and 2363/22. The effective_date is the date stated in this gazette; the currently applicable general rate is 18% from 2024-01-01 under Gazette 2363/22.

summary: This order set VAT on imports and supplies covered by subparagraph (b) at 15% from 1 September 2022. As amended by 2300/25 from 7 October 2022, subparagraph (a) also includes a 0% rate for imported or supplied sanitary towels (pads) and tampons; however, Gazette 2363/22 rescinded this order and replaced the subparagraph (b) rate with 18% from 1 January 2024.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses", "consumers (indirectly, through prices)"]
notes: The position is stated as amended by Gazette 2300/25 and Gazette 2363/22. This gazette's 15% rate was superseded when Gazette 2363/22 rescinded Gazette 2295/08 with effect from 2024-01-01 and set the relevant subparagraph (b) rate at 18%.

summary: The Order defines the specific area where a casino business may operate as the place or premises identified in the casino licence issued under the Act. It takes effect on 1 September 2022 and provides the location basis for licensed casino operations.
audience: ["casino licence holders"]

summary: These regulations set the application and renewal process for casino licences, including a licence fee of Rs. 500 million for each five-year period and a 60-day application window for existing operators. Casino licence holders must appoint compliance officers, prevent unlawful conduct and entry by people under 21, keep specified financial and gaming records, prepare and audit annual accounts, and submit audited accounts to the Minister. The rules also allow licences to be refused, have conditions added, or be cancelled for non-compliance.
audience: ["casino licence holders and applicants"]
notes: Regulation 2(2) measures the 60-day deadline for existing operators from the date of these regulations, 31 August 2022. The document does not include a separate general commencement clause.

summary: From 7 October 2022, imports and domestic supplies of sanitary towels (pads) and tampons under H.S. Code 9619.00.10 are subject to VAT at 0%. The order also continues the VAT rates for specified imported goods listed in the schedule to Gazette Notification No. 2095/20.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses", "consumers (indirectly, through prices)"]
notes: This order amends the order published in Gazette Notification No. 2282/26, which it states was last amended by Gazette Notification No. 2295/08.

summary: From 1 April 2022, financial institutions calculating banking-business profits may not deduct specific debt-claim provisions for the listed categories, including loans to associates, persons outside Sri Lanka and employees, or Stage 1 and Stage 2 credit facilities. They must maintain records of specific debt-claim provisions separately for Stage 1, 2 and 3 facilities using the prescribed format. This notice rescinds Gazette Extraordinary No. 2064/57 from the same date.
audience: ["income taxpayers"]
notes: The document specifically targets persons and financial institutions making specific provisions for debt claims in banking business. The supplied Act-level audience candidates do not include financial institutions, so the closest permitted audience classification is income taxpayers.

summary: The Commissioner General of Inland Revenue has specified the return form for Social Security Contribution Levy. Businesses liable for the levy must submit a completed return for each quarter beginning on or after 1 October 2022, by the 20th day of the month following that quarter. The form records monthly turnover, tax calculations and credits, and warns that penalties may apply for incorrect or late returns and non-payment.
audience: ["businesses liable to the Social Security Contribution Levy"]
notes: The document contains inconsistent spellings of the Commissioner General’s name: the order names Don Ranjith Sisira Kumara Hapuarachchi, while the signature block states Don Ranjith Sisirakumara Hapuarachchi.

summary: From 1 January 2023, employers must withhold employment-income tax using different tax tables for regular pay, lump sums, terminal benefits, multiple or secondary employments, and other specified payments. Employees with more than one employment must nominate a Primary Employment and provide declarations and, when changing jobs, previous withholding certificates. Employers must file annual employee payment and tax details, issue withholding certificates, and keep payroll and tax records for at least five years.
audience: ["employers", "withholding agents", "income taxpayers"]
notes: The document refers to Tax Tables 01–07, but their rates and detailed contents are not included in the supplied text; it says they are available on the Inland Revenue Department web portal.

summary: The order adds a new category to the stamp-duty schedule for leases of land within the Colombo Port City Economic Commission’s area of authority. It covers leases by the Commission where the lessee does not pay the lease premium, rent or other consideration in cash to the Government or the Commission, under an agreement to which the Government is a party; the treatment applies from the date the Port City Commission Act came into force.
audience: ["parties to qualifying leases of land within the Colombo Port City Economic Commission\u2019s area of authority", "notaries handling qualifying lease instruments"]
notes: The order does not state the calendar date on which the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act came into force, so no effective date is reported. The document adds the category to the existing Schedule but does not reproduce the Schedule heading or expressly describe the treatment as an exemption; the practical effect is inferred from the Stamp Duty order context.

summary: From 1 October 2022, this order sets out how VAT on the supply of financial services must be calculated, including the treatment of profits, employee remuneration, economic depreciation, VAT and SSCL. Businesses must separately identify non-financial services where they keep certified separate accounts, or apportion value addition based on turnover, and submit specified accounts and schedules with the annual return. It rescinds Gazette Extraordinary No. 1868/10 with effect from the same date.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses supplying financial services, including registered specified institutions"]
notes: The supplied document text ends partway through the reconciliation table at “Total”, so any requirements appearing after that point could not be assessed.

summary: Additional classes of resident individuals must register under Section 102 of the Inland Revenue Act, unless they were already registered when this notice was issued. From 1 June 2023, this includes specified professionals, business registrants, certain vehicle and property owners, some employees, building-plan applicants, and individuals earning specified amounts from services in Sri Lanka; from 1 January 2024, it also covers individuals aged 18 or over who are not in Part A.
audience: ["Resident individual income taxpayers in the listed categories"]
notes: The notice provides two effective dates: Part A applies from 1 June 2023 and Part B applies from 1 January 2024. It does not state a registration deadline.

summary: From 1 January 2024, the VAT rate is 18% on imports and supplies of goods and on supplies of services, except for goods covered by paragraph 1(b)(a) of the earlier order. This amends Gazette 2282/26 and rescinds Gazette 2295/08 from the same date, so VAT-registered businesses must apply the revised rate to affected transactions.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses"]
notes: Amends Extraordinary Gazette Notification No. 2282/26 and rescinds No. 2295/08, both with effect from 1 January 2024. The document refers to goods covered by sub-paragraph (a) without reproducing that provision; its treatment therefore depends on the earlier order.

summary: From 1 April 2024, the regulation requires specified government registries, government contracting officers, financial institutions and the Colombo Stock Exchange to regularly provide detailed information to the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue. The information covers property and lease transactions, companies and shareholders, vehicles, government contracts, bank accounts and loans, and investments and securities transactions. The Commissioner General will separately notify each person or institution when its reporting must begin; information not previously maintained must be started from 1 July 2024.
audience: ["income taxpayers", "withholding agents", "employers"]
notes: The direct reporting parties listed in the regulation are mainly government institutions, registries, financial institutions and the Colombo Stock Exchange, but these are not included in the supplied audience candidates. The audience therefore remains at the Act-level candidates. Although the regulation comes into effect on 1 April 2024, the CGIR must separately notify each person or institution of its commencement date for furnishing information; Schedule II also states that information not previously maintained is to be maintained from 1 July 2024.

summary: The Commissioner General has specified that tax payments under the Inland Revenue Act must be made only by cash deposit, pay order or bank draft, or through the Online Tax Payments Platform (OTPP). This sets the permitted payment methods for affected tax payments.
audience: ["income taxpayers", "withholding agents", "employers"]
notes: The document does not state an effective date. April 1, 2024 is the date shown for the Inland Revenue Department notice, not an expressly stated commencement date.

summary: From 1 January 2025, withholding agents making payments outside Sri Lanka must withhold the applicable tax on payments to non-residents and obtain a Tax Clearance Certificate before remitting the money, unless the payment falls within the listed exemptions. The rules also require relevant payment details to be reported in withholding tax statements; banks and authorised dealers must collect remittance information and submit monthly schedules to Inland Revenue.
audience: ["withholding agents making outward remittances to non-residents", "income taxpayers who make outward remittances"]
notes: Part of the document, including the Tax Clearance Application and reporting schedule formats, is image-based and the supplied OCR may contain errors. The gazette also expressly binds licensed commercial banks, authorised dealers and certain Government institutes, but these are not among the supplied audience candidates.

summary: From 1 April 2025, stamp duty on instruments for leasing or hiring property is set at Rs. 20 for every Rs. 1,000 (or part) of the total amount payable over the lease or hire term, including any premium. If the term exceeds 20 years, the calculation is limited to the amount payable for the first 20 years. Hire-purchase agreements made under the Consumer Credit Act are charged Rs. 10 for every Rs. 1,000 (or part) of the total amount payable.
audience: ["parties to leases, transfers and other stampable instruments", "notaries"]
notes: This Order deletes and replaces item 9 of the Schedule to the 2006 Order, as previously amended.

summary: From 1 October 2025, VAT will apply to services supplied in Sri Lanka by non-resident persons through electronic platforms, including cloud services, streaming, online marketplaces, digital advertising and similar services. Non-resident suppliers must register when the stated turnover thresholds are exceeded, charge VAT at the applicable rate (currently 18%), remit it by the 20th of the following month, file quarterly returns and keep records. Consumers may see VAT charged on these services, while platform operators must exclude the value of goods or services supplied directly by the original supplier when calculating their own taxable service value.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses", "consumers (indirectly, through prices)"]

summary: From 1 October 2025, VAT refunds for eligible exporters, project suppliers and approved projects will be processed under a new risk-based scheme replacing the former SVAT refund arrangements. Low- and medium-risk claims may be refunded without prior verification, while high-risk claims require verification first. Eligible businesses must keep their RAMIS details, bank information, schedules and supporting records accurate and provide information for checks; the gazette also sets October and November 2025 deadlines for closing outstanding SVAT transactions.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses eligible to claim VAT refunds, including eligible exporters, suppliers to Strategic Development Projects or specified projects, and projects approved under section 22(7)", "VAT-registered Registered Identified Suppliers and Registered Identified Purchasers completing outstanding SVAT transactions"]
notes: The gazette contains several separate transitional deadlines: 15 October 2025, 20 October 2025, 30 October 2025 and 10 November 2025. The scheme's eligibility and risk-rating rules may also depend on records and classifications maintained by the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue.

summary: This gazette specified the tax-invoice format that every VAT-registered person was to use from 1 January 2026, including supplier and purchaser details, invoice numbering, supply information, VAT amounts, payment method, and record retention. As amended by Gazette 2481/22, these specifications were optional until 30 June 2026 and were rescinded from 1 July 2026; a replacement tax-invoice format applies from that date.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses"]
notes: Gazette 2481/22 rescinds the specifications issued under Gazette 2463/05 with effect from 1 July 2026 and introduces a replacement format effective from that date. The effective_date shown is the date stated in this gazette, as required, while the summary reflects the later amended position.

summary: This notice requires every VAT-registered business to issue tax invoices using the specified format, including supplier and purchaser details, TINs, invoice numbering, supply details, VAT amounts and payment information. As amended by Gazette 2500/106, these requirements apply from October 1, 2026, rather than July 1, 2026; the earlier optional format under Gazette 2463/05 is rescinded from that amended effective date.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses"]
notes: The original notice states an effective date of July 1, 2026, but Gazette 2500/106 amends it to October 1, 2026 and leaves all other matters unchanged. The effective_date field follows the date stated in this document, while the summary reflects the amended position.

summary: As amended by Gazette 2500/106, the prescribed format and specifications for tax invoices issued by every registered person under the VAT Act apply from 1 October 2026, instead of 1 July 2026. All other requirements in Gazette 2481/22 remain unchanged.
audience: ["VAT-registered businesses"]
notes: This gazette amends Gazette 2481/22. The effective date in the earlier notice is changed from 1 July 2026 to 1 October 2026; all other matters remain unchanged.
